central_unknown: Whether to use Final Fix or Limitless this weekend, and which Ferrari driver (Leclerc or Hamilton) to captain — qualifying will decide everything at a track with virtually zero overtaking.

budget_tiers.core: Leclerc (2x), Hamilton or Antonelli, Ferrari constructor, Mercedes constructor
Leclerc (2x), Hamilton, Verstappen, Antonelli, Russell, Ferrari, Mercedes

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: Consensus pick across all channels. Home race specialist, won Driver of the Day the last two years (worth 10 bonus points), Ferrari 1-2 in both FP1 and FP2, P1 in FP1 and P2 in FP2. Four front-row starts in last five Monaco GPs. Dirt cheap relative to Antonelli, enabling budget flexibility for Final Fix pivot.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: P2 in FP1, P1 in FP2. Brilliant form since Canada. Even cheaper than Leclerc. If Hamilton wins his first race for Ferrari at Monaco, he likely bags Driver of the Day instead. Multiple creators flag him as a viable alternative captain.

buy.name: Franco Colapinto
buy.note: Consensus set-and-forget. Positive points in every race this season, needs only -14 points to avoid price fall and -6 for max rise. 65% ownership in top 500. Q3 upside with Alpine's improving pace. Pure budget enabler.

buy.name: Valtteri Bottas
buy.note: Dirt cheap budget enabler. Needs just 1 point to gain 0.6M. Only two career retirements at Monaco. Just has to survive. Multiple creators recommend him.

buy.name: Lance Stroll
buy.note: Budget building candidate — needs -8 points for max 0.6M price rise. Usually keeps it clean. Back-to-back finishes suggest vibration/reliability issues resolved. Some creators nervous about Aston Martin reliability. Short-term 1-2 race punt.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Top 10 in FP2, Audi looked like best-of-rest in P8-P10 area. Quali average of 11th gives Q3 upside. Needs 3 points to avoid price fall, 8 for max rise. FanAmp concerned about Audi reliability and poor race starts at a no-overtaking track.

buy.name: Oliver Bearman
buy.note: P10 in FP2, Haas very reliable. Solid budget balancing option with some points upside. Needs 8 points to avoid price fall — tight at Monaco but achievable if he qualifies well.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Consensus hold/buy-for-Barcelona rather than Monaco. Needs 11 points to avoid drop — very hard at Monaco. His Miami DNF drops off his 3-race average after Monaco. Excellent buy candidate for Spain where he'll be at top of price gain list at a high-overtake circuit.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: Needs only -4 points to lose just 0.2M. Historic Monaco podium in 2023 but P17 in FP2 this weekend. More of a hold than a buy.

avoid: Alex Albon — negative score trajectory, needs 13 points to avoid price fall, very unlikely at Monaco
Sergio Perez — brake fire in FP2, expected -0.6M price drop, sell candidate
Fernando Alonso — crashed in FP1, expected -0.6M drop, DNF risk with Aston Martin reliability
Nico Hulkenberg — toxic asset, needs 25+ points to avoid price fall despite flashes of pace
Arvid Lindblad — needs 25+ points to avoid price fall, unusable
Isaac Hadjar — crashed in FP1, half a second off Antonelli, budget not looking good
Pierre Gasly — needs 25+ points to avoid price fall, sell
McLaren drivers (Norris/Piastri) — reliability issue for Norris in FP2, both outside top 5 all day, well behind Ferrari/Mercedes/Verstappen

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Strong consensus that Limitless is excellent at Monaco. Big delta swing because most managers can't afford Hamilton+Leclerc+Verstappen+Mercedes+Ferrari together. Viable even with 1-2 toxic assets (Albon, Perez) dropping in value — creators agree you come out ahead on points. Optimal Limitless team: Leclerc (2x), Hamilton, Verstappen, Antonelli, Russell + Ferrari + Mercedes. ZachGP says don't use if you have both Albon AND Alonso. Multiple creators note very few viable Limitless weekends remain (Silverstone, Hungary at best).

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Excellent candidate weekend. Start with Antonelli (cheaper, likely price gain regardless), then swap to Leclerc or Hamilton if they take pole. Saves a transfer and preserves budget. However, ReinFantasy argues saving Final Fix for later-season grid penalties (e.g., engine penalties at Monza) may be higher value. FanAmp and ZachGP lean toward using it. F1FantasyPolePosition comfortable using it. Disagreement exists but consensus is it's a strong play if needed.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No creator recommends Wildcard this week. Better saved for a bigger team overhaul, possibly around the summer break or when grid penalties shuffle the order.

watch_items: FP3 and qualifying results will determine Final Fix usage — if Leclerc or Hamilton takes pole, swap from Antonelli immediately
McLaren reliability: Norris retired in FP2 with a failure, Piastri also slow — complete sell on McLaren constructor and drivers this weekend
Audi reliability at Monaco: Bortoleto looked fast but Audi has poor race starts and reliability concerns — a DNF at a no-overtake track is devastating
Perez brake fire in FP2 — monitor whether his car is repaired and race-ready, though he's a sell regardless
Driver of the Day: worth 10 points at a low-scoring track — Leclerc has won it two years running at Monaco, but Hamilton could steal it with a first Ferrari win
Overtaking data: only 4 overtakes in 2025, 17 in 2024 — new smaller 2026 cars may allow slightly more, but don't bank on overtake-dependent B-tier strategies
Weather: 25% rain chance on Sunday — rain at Monaco would completely reshuffle the order and reward those who held Final Fix
arc: Monaco is the tightest budget weekend of the season and a defining moment for chip usage. After this race, the calendar shifts to Barcelona (Spain GP), a high-speed, high-overtake circuit where Mercedes are expected to reassert dominance and McLaren should bounce back. Liam Lawson becomes a priority buy for Spain as his Miami DNF drops off his rolling average. Managers who used Limitless here can rebuild budget through Spain and Austria with Colapinto, Stroll, and Bottas. Those saving Final Fix should watch for engine/battery grid penalties emerging around Silverstone and the summer break, as multiple teams (Russell, McLaren) have already used spare components early. The key post-Monaco question is whether to pivot back to McLaren or stay heavy on Ferrari — Barcelona's track characteristics should clarify the pecking order.
